title: From a roll of steel to a car
_story: Steve crafts a minecart from iron in one click. Ismaeel follows a real car through a factory: a coil of steel, pressed panels, robots welding with sparks, paint, the assembly line, and a test drive.
_stepChain: crafting vs a factory → steel coil → press shapes panels → robots weld → estimate the welds (about 5,000) → paint layers (rust) → assembly line adds battery, motor, seats, windows, wheels → tap parts → test drive → 4 wheels × 6 cars

talk.ask: What are the main jobs in a car factory?
talk.goodAnswer: pressing steel into shapes, welding them together, painting, then adding all the parts on the assembly line, and testing.

talk.ask: Why do factories use robots for welding?
talk.goodAnswer: robots don't get tired and put every weld in exactly the right place, thousands of times a day; people do the jobs that need careful hands and eyes.

handsOn: Next time you're in a car park, look closely at a car door edge with a grown-up. Can you see where two pieces of metal are joined? Count the wheels on 3 cars.

narration.speaker: steve
narration.text: In my world, I make a minecart from 5 iron ingots, and it pops out in one go. But a real car has thousands of parts. How do people put a car together?
Most of a car's body is made of a strong metal called steel. It arrives at the factory as a giant roll of thin steel, called a coil.
The steel is cut into flat sheets. Then a huge machine called a press squashes each sheet into a shape, like pressing play dough into a mould: doors, a roof, sides, a bonnet.
Robots join the pieces with electricity. It melts a tiny spot of metal, which cools and holds the pieces tight. Each spot is called a weld.
The robots make weld after weld, all over the body.

question.prompt: How many welds do you think one car has?
question.reveal: About 5,000 welds in a family car! Every one in exactly the right place.

narration.text: Steel goes brown and crumbly if it gets wet. That's called rust. So the body is painted in layers: one that stops rust, then the colour, then a clear shiny coat on top.
Then the car rolls slowly along a moving line. People and machines add the parts one by one: the battery, the motor, the seats, the windows and the wheels. That's called an assembly line.
Tap a part to hear what it does.

parts.label: Battery
parts.narration: The big flat battery under the floor stores the electricity.

parts.label: Motor
parts.narration: The motor uses the electricity to turn the wheels.

parts.label: Body
parts.narration: The welded, painted steel body keeps everyone safe inside.

narration.speaker: steve
narration.text: Last, every car is tested: the lights, the brakes, and a drive. Off it goes!
A factory puts 4 wheels on every car.

0.hint: Every car gets its own 4 wheels. Count 4 at a time.
0.say: You added 6 and 4. Count 4 for each car: 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24.

2.say: 20 is 5 cars. One more car adds 4: 24.

rule.text: Press it, weld it, paint it, build it, test it.
rule.ask: Can you say how a car is made? Say it out loud. Then tap the eye.
rule.spoken: Steel is pressed into shapes, welded together, painted, then the parts are added on the assembly line, and every car is tested.
